headlines.html: SpaceX unveils Starmind formation concept: The company outlined an architecture linking about 10 AI satellites over high-bandwidth connections for shared computing. Up to 1 million satellites is a deployment target, and the newly released video depicts a concept rather than a finalized design. — (TESLARATI·PCMag)

2026-10-08.summary_html:
① SpaceX (TESLARATI·PCMag, 10/6) — (2026-10-06) Michael Nicolls described a concept involving about 10 Starmind satellites flying in close formation, linked at roughly 10 Tbps. The plan is to pool their computing resources to run AI models jointly. The new video illustrates a concept subject to change, and the application for up to 1 million satellites remains under FCC review. The announcement does not constitute an orbital demonstration or deployment approval. The significance of this announcement lies less in the satellite count than in the approach to combining multiple satellites into a single computing resource. For the concept to work, the satellites must maintain both high-speed links and precise formation flying. SpaceX’s accompanying emphasis on sharing orbital and maneuver data can also be seen as a prerequisite for operations at this scale. The next question is whether orbital testing validates the concept and its target bandwidth.

headlines.html: Satlyt raises $8 million for orbital AI software: The company is expanding deployment of software that processes data aboard other operators’ satellites — (Space in Africa·Company announcement)

South Korea targets 2028 demonstration of a 100 kg-class space data center: The K-Moonshot program director outlined plans to use Nuri’s seventh launch and test domestically developed AI chips — (Edaily)

2026-10-05.summary_html:
① Satlyt (Space in Africa, 10/1) — (2026-10-01) Satlyt raised $8 million in seed funding led by Non Sibi Ventures. The company deploys AI software aboard other operators’ satellites to reduce the volume of data transmitted to the ground. Its next demonstration will run two applications for research and image processing on a single satellite, with pooling computing resources across multiple satellites a longer-term goal.

② K-Moonshot (Edaily, 10/1) — (2026-10-01) Lee Chun-woo, program director for space, said South Korea plans to develop a 100 kg-class small data center by 2028 and demonstrate it on Nuri’s seventh launch. The initiative aims to test domestically developed AI inference chips and solar cells, then scale up to a medium-sized system in 2031. Only part of the development budget has been allocated, leaving additional funding to be secured. The two developments suggest that software and component demonstrations are opening more routes into the orbital data center market. Opportunities could emerge not only for companies building entire satellites, but also for developers using onboard computers and suppliers whose components have proven their performance in space. Future orbital operating results will determine whether these funding rounds and development targets translate into services for customers.
